course_title: Identifying and Assisting Students at Risk
course_description:
Welcome to EDUC7001 On the Edge: Identifying and Assisting Students At-Risk.ﾠIn this course, students will develop their knowledge and skills to identify, describe and supportﾠa range of school-based emotional and behavioural concernsﾠthat occur in the school-aged population (6-18ﾠyears). Social, environmental, and medical inter-agency sources of the concerns are examined, via contemporary theory frames and analytical tools. Skills in identification andﾠassessment of, and support for, specific concerns will be developed using a problem-based approach.

This course may not be offered in person if the enrolment is less than 10 students.

course_aims: The aim of the course is to develop the knowledge and skills of teachers, learning support teachers, guidance counsellors, educational psychologists, social workers, counsellors, school administrators, and others in schools in recognising, describing, and supporting emotional and behavioural difficulties of children and adolescents at risk.

learning_outcomes.description: Increase your knowledge, understanding and skills in relation to the identification of children and adolescents at risk.
Increase your knowledge, understanding and skills in relation to the assessment of children and adolescents at risk, specifically your observation, interview, and screening skills.
Increase your knowledge, understanding and skills in relation to support for children and adolescents at risk.
Develop a working knowledge of major issues and approaches described in the literature, as it relates to the education of and support for students at risk.

assessment_details.due_date: Powerpoint Presentation due by 14:00 24/08/2026 - 24/08/2026 Oral Simulation at scheduled time 24/08/2026 - 24/08/2026
assessment_details.task_description: Work through the materials on the EDUC7001 BLACKBOARD site that refer to the case, ROBERT PAGE, a 14-year-old at-risk male high school student. For the task, assume the role of your intended profession (e.g., teacher, guidance counsellor, social worker, educational psychologist, learning support teacher) where Robert Page attends school. As a stakeholder in the support team of Robert Page, you have been requested to present an overview of Robert’s case to the support team, discussing what has happened up to this point in his life to bring him to the attention of professionals. This assessment aims to develop professionally relevant skills, to convey a deep understanding of the case of Robert Page. You will present a clear understanding of the risk and protective factors that may be influencing Robert’s behaviour and why these factors, according to literature, may be placing him at risk, or providing some protection for him. Refer to the EDUC7001 Criteria Sheet Assignment 1 for the specific requirements for each section of the assignment and how the assignment will be assessed. This live online oral simulation will be video recorded to ensure there is an accurate record of your performance. Recordings will be retained for 12 months on a secure UQ system in accordance with UQ assessment policy. For this online oral, you will require a working webcam, headphones, and you will be required to reveal the room during the oral. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.task_description: You are to respond to a series of 4 mini tasks that demonstrates your understanding of core theoretical knowledge, key content, and concepts from course lectures and readings. These exercises are designed to help you apply core theoretical knowledge to a real-world student case and develop critical thinking skills and build your confidence in theory application. Each task has a 500-word allowance and is worth 5% of the overall course grade. Tasks will be released progressively following the completion of relevant lecture content. You will have until 2pm the following Monday to post your response. All tasks will be assessed using a pass/fail rubric, with a focus on demonstrating understanding and application of key course concepts. Each of the tasks is graded as a pass/fail. Students must successfully achieve a pass to receive the 5% allocated to each mini task in the series for a total of 20%. Read full task description Hide full task description
